brief: docs/briefs/52-kat-pi-agent.md follow-up: does a larger per-reply cap (32768 vs 8192 tokens) rescue KAT's Eval B cases that ended on the cap?
machine: M1 Max 32 GB, user's normal apps open (swap 13-15 GB in use)
setup: tools/pi_agent_eval.py run --arm kat --max-tokens 32768 --cases <KAT's 11 cap cases from results/20261123T174500Z-kat-pi>; same sandbox, 30 min / 40 tool-call limits, temp 0.8, top-p 1.0, thinking off. Label kat-mt32768.

not_run.1598_E-python3: Metal OOM three times (contexts >31k tokens next to the user's apps); counted as a fail below

attribution: Only 2 of the 4 passes used a reply over 8192 tokens (1604_D-python3 9.9k, 1622_C-python3 16.1k): those are real cap rescues. The other 2 passed with short replies, i.e. a different sample at temperature 0.8, which the 8192 run could also have drawn; no 8192 control rerun was done.
estimate: KAT through pi with a 32k cap: 17/30 + 2 cap rescues = 19/30 attributable (21/30 counting the 2 resample passes, which overstates it: only failed cases were rerun). 4 cases still ran into even the 32k cap: on hard problems KAT reasons without stopping.
costs: rescued cases took 320-534 s; 32k runaway replies take 13-15 min each and drove the three OOMs
qwen_pi_adapter_cap_rerun: stopped by the user's choice after 3 of 7 cases (focus on KAT); not scored
recommendation: Raise KAT's reply cap to 16384, not 32768: it covers both real rescues (9.9k, 16.1k) and halves the time and memory a runaway reply can take. Applied in tools/delegate.py (one-shot helper, was 8192).
